# Day 1: Maps and questions

## Teacher page

### Before class
Prepare Maps A/B, Trail Map, question strips, map card, question board and record sheet. Keep key-01.md teacher-only. Send the bilingual family note. Keep the Visitor Case hidden until Exit ticket. Say the people and Trail Map are made up.

### The day
#### 7 min. Hook
Review grade 3: physical map shows land and water; political map shows borders. Show A and B, ours, dated November 23, 2026; geographic data: Source 1A, Source 1B and Source 1C.

**Ask.** [[s01-P1-1]] Expect visible differences. Pairs take two simultaneous 45-second turns. Everyone may pass publicly. Post: "What can a map tell us, and what does it leave out?" Review grade 3's two readings of a word: useful can mean different things. Tracing water and comparing borders need different information.

#### 6 min. Retrieval
Review grade 3's title, legend, north arrow, cardinal directions, bar length and whole bars. Alone: [[s01-P1-2]] [[s01-P1-3]] [[s01-P1-4]] [[s01-P1-5]]. Read the questions aloud if needed. This map is made up. Note errors A, B and C without grading.

#### 10 min. Supporting questions
Review grade 3's big question, supporting question and question board. A big question needs several smaller answers. Model [[s01-K1-1]] after children suggest wording.

[[steps:s01-K1-1]]

Pairs sort [[s01-P1-6]]. Co-write five questions using the useful strips. Keep their meanings: map parts, distance, choosing scale, boundaries and grid. Tag answer-days 4, 6, 8, 11 and 13. Explain that missing information can prevent a reader's needed use.

#### 12 min. Supported work
Each child attempts [[s01-P1-7]]. Hear a rotating six at 45 seconds each, 4.5 minutes total; record names. Others work simultaneously. Collect annotations for a written cue tomorrow. Review the four-part map card; keep it available. Ungraded retrieval and sorting stay in the folder.

#### 5 min. Exit ticket
Uncover the new made-up Visitor Case. Children work alone: [[s01-X1]] on the half slip, then [[s01-P1-E]] in the Exit box. Collect both. After class, allow 30 children times 30 seconds, 15 minutes, for marking. Review the component record: use only shown, shown with help, not yet seen, one cell per component. Access support is not content help. Return day 2; save copies for day 14.

### Other rooms
Without a printer, draw A, B and Trail Map on the board. Children copy only needed marks. Give the Visitor Case on fresh paper at exit time.

### At home
**Swap.** No printer: copy the maps and use scrap paper. No chart: keep questions together.
**Skip.** The class board and rotating group.
- **7 min. Compare.** Look at A and B. Use [[s01-P1-1]]. **Say.** "What differs?" Expect land and water versus borders.
- **6 min. Remember.** Your child completes the four Trail Map tasks.
- **10 min. Questions.** Sort [[s01-P1-6]]. Help word smaller questions. Keep the question list.
- **7 min. Use a detail.** Your child completes [[s01-P1-7]]. **Say.** "What does that detail help find?" Expect a use tied to a visible detail.
- **5 min. Exit ticket.** Reveal the Visitor Case. Your child completes [[s01-X1]] and [[s01-P1-E]] alone. Discuss afterward.

### Shorter or longer
Shorter: hear three of the six today; retain the question sort and exit. Longer: try another wording for the map-parts question.

### Words and supports
Review: legend means map key. Review: supporting question means a smaller question helping answer the big one. Enlarge labels; accept dictation without adding ideas.

### Tomorrow
Day 2 reads rivers, lakes and oceans. Return day 1's annotations and both exit responses. If many showed error J or error M, repair the dominant gap in five minutes. Otherwise repair retrieval error A, error B or error C. The second gap gets a small group during Supported work.

### Credit
Ours. Geographic outlines and selected labels use public-domain data from Source 1A, Source 1B and Source 1C.

## Student page
### Side 1
**I can ask smaller questions about maps.**

**Physical Map A: North America.** Land and water. Locator only, not for measuring.
